title: Advisory triage framework for optimization requests (batching/caching, quantization, routing)
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Background: Enterprise customers are increasingly submitting ad hoc optimization requests asking for help tuning batching/caching knobs, choosing quantization profiles, or designing routing policies to meet strict latency/cost/SLO goals. Current intake is inconsistent: some requests land as support tickets, some as Solutions Engineering (SE) engagements, and some as engineering feature requests, which causes duplicated triage effort and slow time-to-value.

Goals: Create a pragmatic triage framework and intake flow that routes optimization/advisory requests to the appropriate path (self-serve guidance, SE advisory, or engineering initiative), reduces turnaround time, and captures signal to prioritize product work (e.g., dashboard improvements, automated suggestions, new knobs).

Scope: Non-bug customer requests focused on performance optimization and advisory assistance across three areas: (1) batching & caching configuration, (2) quantization and model variant recommendations, (3) routing policies and fallback strategies. Excludes security incidents, platform outages, and feature bugs.

Proposed solution summary: 1) Standardize an "Optimization Intake" form for PM/SE/Support to capture workload profile, current performance metrics, business goal (latency vs cost vs accuracy), privacy constraints, and preferred engagement level. 2) Apply a lightweight scoring rubric (impact x frequency x compliance complexity x effort) to route requests into three paths: Fast Path (self-serve docs + config templates), Advisory Path (SE consult + runbook + one-off configs), Product Path (prioritized engineering project). 3) Track outcomes in a triage board and tag signals for product roadmap (e.g., repeated requests for automatic prefix caching, need for auto-quantization recommendations).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form created and published in Confluence and connected to the internal intake URL
Scoring rubric documented with threshold values that map to Fast/Advisory/Product paths
Triage board (Linear) configured to automatically label and route based on rubric output
Pilot completed with 3 enterprise customers and feedback captured; measurable reduction in advisory lead time (target: 50% faster)
Clear handoff templates for SE -> Eng for Product Path with required artifacts (sample workload, logs, perf traces)

intake_form_fields: Willingness for SE engagement (none / limited / full)
Attachments: perf traces, sample workload, example prompts
triage_rubric: Impact: estimated cost or latency improvement potential (Low/Medium/High)
Frequency: number of customers/occurrences requesting same guidance
Effort: SE minutes or Eng story points
Route mapping: Fast Path = Low impact, low effort; Advisory Path = Medium impact or enterprise customer; Product Path = High impact + high engineering effort
paths_and_slAs: Fast Path: self-serve docs + config templates. SLA: acknowledge within 2 business days. Ownership: Docs + Developer Experience.
Advisory Path: SE engagement with runbook and 1-2 consult sessions. SLA: respond within SLA based on contract tier. Ownership: Solutions Engineering.
Product Path: Eng project created with standard PRD and perf harness. SLA: triage meeting within 3 business days; engineering prioritization follows roadmap process. Ownership: Product + Eng
handoff_requirements: Minimal reproducible workload (token-level traces or synthetic script)
Current infra config (instance types, GPU sizes, batching settings, cache TTL)
Observed metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, token cost estimates)
Customer success contact and acceptance criteria
pilot_plan: Select 3 enterprise customers (one hosted, one dedicated, one private) - target customers identified by Marco Alvarez
Run intake flow for incoming optimization requests over 4 weeks
Measure time-to-first-action and resolution path; collect customer satisfaction survey
Iterate on rubric thresholds and adjust routing rules in Linear
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SE capacity overloaded if many medium-impact requests. Mitigation: temporarily increase Fast Path docs and add training sessions for Customer Success.
Risk: Missing workload artifacts delays engineering triage. Mitigation: make artifacts required for Product Path and provide sampling script in intake.
Risk: Confidential customer data restricts advisory. Mitigation: offer on-prem SE sessions or sign necessary NDAs and mark request as high compliance complexity
